intended_object: A separator (also called a generator) in a category C: an object G such that the corepresentable functor C(G, −) is faithful. That is, for any parallel pair f, g : X ⟶ Y, if h ≫ f = h ≫ g for every h : G ⟶ X, then f = g. Taken from the docstring.
explanation: The definition says that the singleton object property {G} is separating. In `ObjectProperty.IsSeparating P`, for all f, g : X ⟶ Y, if h ≫ f = h ≫ g for every G' with P G' and every h : G' ⟶ X, then f = g. With P the singleton {G}, the only such G' is G itself. So the condition becomes: h ≫ f = h ≫ g for all h : G ⟶ X implies f = g. This is exactly faithfulness of C(G, −), the standard notion of a separator. It is stated for an arbitrary category, which is its natural generality. This is Mathlib's own definition of the notion, so there is no separate counterpart to cite.
